name: spatial
note: IS THE SPATIAL MIXER THE PROBLEM? The diagnostic pattern this sweep responds to: our trunk BEATS EEGNet by 6.8 points subject-dependently and LOSES to it cross-subject. A weak architecture loses in both regimes; one that wins within-subject and loses across subjects is spending capacity on subject-specific structure. The nuisance ratio measured that directly -- between-subject over within-subject feature variance on held-out subjects ranked four arms in exactly inverse order of their accuracy, and the subject-dependent champion scored worst of all at 1.679. The prime suspect is a single component: the trunk mixes C electrodes into 88 spatial filters, a 4x over-complete basis, unconstrained and bias-free, which bought +0.37 (n.s.) for 4x the parameters. An unconstrained over-complete spatial basis fitted on one person is exactly what encodes anatomy rather than task, and EEGNet constrains its spatial convolution with max-norm for this reason. This sweep varies ONLY the spatial stage -- width, and whether its rows are norm-constrained -- holding the rest of the trunk, the recipe and the folds fixed. A win for a NARROWER or CONSTRAINED mixer would make the model smaller and better at once, which is the signature of a real diagnosis rather than a tuning knob. A flat result exonerates the mixer and moves suspicion to the pooling operator and the absent normalization.

arms.name: sp88
arms.prediction: the champion width, 4x over-complete on a 22-electrode montage and ~1.4x on Cho2017's 64. The reference every other row is paired against.

arms.name: sp64
arms.prediction: square mixer on Cho2017 -- a change of basis rather than an expansion

arms.name: sp32
arms.prediction: under-complete: forced to discard directions. If this MATCHES sp88, the extra width was never buying task-relevant structure.

arms.name: sp16
arms.prediction: aggressively narrow, near EEGNet's spatial budget. Expect a drop; where it starts dropping locates how many spatial directions the task actually needs.

arms.name: sp88_maxnorm
arms.prediction: THE arm this sweep exists for. Same width, rows constrained to unit L2 -- EEGNet's own regulariser on its spatial stage. If width is fine but freedom is the problem, this wins without shrinking anything.

arms.name: sp32_maxnorm
arms.prediction: both levers together; the smallest configuration that could plausibly win

arms.name: nomix
arms.prediction: no electrode mixing at all -- the published trunk, which defers every spatial decision to the attention block. The floor, and the control that says how much the mixer is worth in total.

arms.name: eegnet
arms.prediction: the external reference, so this sweep can be read without cross-referencing another results directory
